summary.para: Sets construction variables for the &javah; tool. If a javah command is available (Java 9 and earlier), the &b-link-JavaH; builder uses it; otherwise it uses javac -h, which has been able to generate JNI headers since Java 8.
Changed in version NEXT_RELEASE: added the fallback to javac -h.

Builds C header and source files for implementing Java native methods. The target can be either a directory in which the header files will be written, or a header file name which will contain all of the definitions. The source can be the names of .class files, the names of .java files to be compiled into .class files by calling the &b-link-Java; builder method, or the objects returned from the &b-Java; builder method.
When javac -h is used, the source must be .java files (or class nodes for which the Java sources are known), since javac generates the headers while compiling.

If the construction variable &cv-link-JAVACLASSDIR; is set, either in the environment or in the call to the &b-JavaH; builder method itself, then the value of the variable will be stripped from the beginning of any .class file names.
summary.example_commands:
# builds java_native.h classes = env.Java(target="classdir", source="src") env.JavaH(target="java_native.h", source=classes)
# builds include/package_foo.h and include/package_bar.h env.JavaH(target="include", source=["package/foo.class", "package/bar.class"])
# builds export/foo.h and export/bar.h env.JavaH( target="export", source=["classes/foo.class", "classes/bar.class"], JAVACLASSDIR="classes", )

note.para: The javah command was removed from the JDK in Java 10 (see Java Enhancement Proposal JEP 313). When no javah command can be found, the &b-JavaH; builder uses javac -h instead, which is available in Java 8 and later. In that case only classes which declare native methods produce a header file, but the header files are still declared as targets so their dependencies are tracked normally.

If javah is found on the system, it is used even if the configured &cv-link-JAVAC; is from a newer JDK; this preserves the pre-Java-10 behaviour. To force the javac -h mechanism, set &cv-link-JAVAH; to the &cv-link-JAVAC; command. If you previously worked around the removal of &javah; by setting &cv-link-JAVAH; to javac and adding -h to &cv-link-JAVAHFLAGS;, you no longer need to do so: the option is now added automatically, and leaving it in place will produce a duplicate-option error.

javac -h always writes one header file per class into a directory, so it cannot combine all of the definitions into a single output file. Using a file as the target of &b-JavaH; is only supported by the legacy javah command.

summary.para: The Java generator for C header and stub files. Defaults to javah if that command is available, otherwise to javac. When javac is used, its -h option generates the headers.

The command line used to generate C header and stub files from Java classes. Any options specified in the &cv-link-JAVAHFLAGS; construction variable are included on this command line. If &cv-link-JAVAH; is javac, the command line compiles the Java sources and writes the headers to the target directory.
The string displayed when C header and stub files are generated from Java classes. If this is not set, then &cv-link-JAVAHCOM; (the command line) is displayed.
General options passed to the C header and stub file generator for Java classes. When &cv-link-JAVAH; is javac, these are passed to javac; the -h option itself is added automatically.
